title: Design System: Nimiq Pay Mini Apps

body.purpose: Descriptions and interstitial copy; secondary at 82% alpha, tertiary ~70%.

narrative.overview: The catalog is a quiet shelf in a dim arcade: the chrome (backgrounds, borders, text) stays near-monochrome — white or Nimiq midnight blue with alpha-tint surfaces — while every mini app glows like its own cabinet. Saturated color enters the page exclusively through the app-type gradients (gold for Nimiq, indigo for EVM, green for 'all') and the apps' own logos. The shelf never competes with the cabinets. The system is playful and tactile, not corporate: every interactive element responds with a spring, because browsing here should feel like an app store, not a SaaS brochure.
keyCharacteristics: Dual-theme via CSS light-dark() — white paper in light, Nimiq midnight blue in dark; every neutral is an alpha tint of ink or white.
Color is earned: saturated gradients belong to app types, never to chrome.
Springy motion (motion-v) with reduced-motion='user' honored globally.
Flat surfaces; shadows exist only as colored glow under gradient elements.

rules.name: The Shelf Rule
rules.body: Chrome is never saturated. Backgrounds, cards, borders, and text use only alpha tints of ink or white. If an element wants color, it must be an app-type gradient or an app's own logo — there is no third source of color.

rules.name: The One Cabinet Rule
rules.body: One gradient CTA per view. Store buttons, browser-fallback links, and secondary actions stay neutral so 'Open in Nimiq Pay' is always the loudest thing on screen.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Mulish does everything. Never introduce a second display face; reach for weight (400 → 600 → 700) and alpha (100% → 82% → 70%) instead.

rules.name: The Glow Rule
rules.body: A shadow must be tinted by the gradient it sits under, or it must belong to a floating overlay. A gray drop shadow on a flat neutral card is forbidden.

dos: Do keep chrome on alpha-tint neutrals (the Shelf Rule); let gradients and app logos be the only saturated color.
Do give every interactive element a spring response (stiffness 320–400, damping 18–30) and rely on MotionConfig reduced-motion='user' to quiet it.
Do use light-dark() pairs for every new color token so both themes ship together.
Do keep exactly one gradient CTA per view (the One Cabinet Rule) — 'Open in Nimiq Pay' always wins.
Do use the focus-ring shortcut (2px Nimiq Orange, offset 2) on anything focusable.
donts: Don't build corporate SaaS landing patterns — hero-metric blocks, identical icon-heading-text card grids, stock-marketing tone.
Don't clutter like a noisy app store: no ad banners, ranking spam, or competing CTAs next to Open-in-Pay.
Don't put gray drop shadows on flat neutral cards; shadows are colored glows under gradients or overlay floats only.
Don't introduce a second font family, gradient text (background-clip: text), glassmorphism, or colored side-stripe borders.
Don't hardcode single-theme colors; a hex without a light-dark() partner breaks the dark theme.

Don't use empty /

for decorative elements — nimiq-css preflight hides empty spans; use
